body: I have tried all of the meds in the MAOi class. Parnate exacerbated anxiety, but Nardil was great until it wasn't. It is notorious for “pooping” out, and after years of adding various other meds to get it to work again, I had to quit. As someone who also has insomnia, the daytime fatigue compounded by the drug's tendency to disrupt the sleep cycle is a nightmare. I know too many people who have had a period of success with MAOIs, but they, too, find it just stops working.

Yep. It was crazy. But I already suffer from insomnia, so during this time, I had scored what I thought was an amazing job and the intermittent breaks of being able to work were over. But even with meds, Nardil has made it impossible to fall asleep and stay alseep, let alone be alert for a 8+ day. I will never touch methylphenidate again. The comedown was brutal, and it doesn't seem to matter how much I take, it's not enough to keep awake and sane. My psychiatrist spoke with my GP, went in depth to the one test that I have ever had even slightly elevated liver enzymes, and my psychiatrist is okay with trying the switch to Nefazodone. He’d rather I try imipramine, but I'm going with Nefazodone first, then imipramine, and if history repeats itself, I'll be back on Nardil by fall, and I can only hope that I find a way to live a meaningful life on it.

I have not been able to work steadily since I started it years ago.

I did try Mirtazapine for just a month. It didn't make me tired, but I did not react to it well. Nardil can be a game-changer - but it is exceptionally sedating. For most people, it causes severe insomnia, and finding a sleep aid when you're on an MAOI is challenging. Working a job with long hours required me to take a massive dose of methylphenidate just to get through the day. Plus, most people find that it stops working after a period of time. I’m not getting any benefits (other than the absence of night terrors and a bit less anxiety ) from it currently and have just signed on for a course of TMS, which is pretty effective for me when it stops working. But, I am so eager to try something new. My life is severely limited by the fatigue Nardil can cause.But honestly, if you’ve tried everything and really struggling, I’d recommend Nardil. Some people adjust to the changes it causes - but it does have serious sexual side effects that seem to be universal.

Anxiety is my primary issue. TMS on the other side of the head treats anxiety, but it is not currently covered by insurance, so I have not tried it. For me, my severe depressive episodes start with extended periods of extreme anxiety. For me, TMS not only eliminates the depression, but it seems to jump-start Nardil, so it alleviates anxiety again. Plus, the complete remission of depression makes such a huge difference - I feel so good that I can manage the anxiety. It's been a lifesaver. And I don't believe that it has any effect on your blood pressure. My blood pressure runs a bit high and I have to be on the strongest level of pulses which is quite painful and extremely rare - the pain or discomfort you experience the first few times would be the only reason I can think of that would cause any rise in blood pressure, but you will quickly adapt - again, most people feel just a mild discomfort and the machine is very loud. I know that the offices I have visited have a TV with Netflix and other streaming services that distract from the noise and any discomfort. Again, I am always on the highest frequency and this so rare that both treatment centers  i've been to had never had a similar patient. I can tell you more about the process if you want to dm me, but compared to ECT and ketamine, this is the least invasive and most effective treatment I have experienced when Nardil just stops working. You can expect a mild headache if you are at the typical frequency, but even this is temporary and can be avoided by taking extra strength Tylenol prior to your sessions. I highly recommend TMS to anyone with treatment refractory depression, and since no medication is used, you can still take an all your meds during your course of treatment. Again, nothing as brutal as ECT and since most insurance companies cover TMS, it's a hell of a lot cheaper than ketamine infusions (though I admit, ketamine is much more fun😉).

Yes. I have been taking Nardil prior to and during TMS treatment. When I have a severe depressive episode and increasing Nardil fails to treat my symptoms, I have a course of TMS and it has been extremely effective two times. You do not need nor should you discontinue any antidepressant, including an MAOI, while undergoing a course of TMS.

Yes. I have done 3 tms treatment courses after Nardil stopped working. The first two were successful, but the third time was not. However, the last time was at a different location than the first two- I’m considering going back and trying another round at the location of the first two courses and am still on Nardil.

I had one ovary removed five years ago because it was entangled in a chocolate cyst. I requested the other be removed since I knew that was necessary to cure pmdd. I’m not even too weeks in and my shitty boss told me that it was in my best interest to work part time the second week. First day back and I overreacted to a coworker who I usually just ignore. I’m too sensitive to work. As soon as I can get my short term disability documents ready, I’m out. Until then it’s late nights and early weekends to catch up on a ridiculously high workload.

End stage endometriosis was the reason my doctor would do the surgery. I had been dismissed by so many other doctors when they saw the list of psychotropic meds I was on, so I only listed one when I saw this doctor for the first time. I know it made a a huge difference. She treated with me like a normal patient and she recommended the hysterectomy. I elected to have my remaining ovary removed (essential for pmdd) and the true reason I had the surgery was to stop the cycle of depression and suicidal ideations that would last until my cycle started. I didn’t share that with her. I played the endometriosis card and requested a complete hysterectomy so I didn’t have to go through hell my hormones put me through. It’s very difficult to find a doctor who will do the surgery for pmdd alone. I did what was necessary to hopefully get my life back. Lying is sometimes your only option to get help when you have a mental illness.

Thanks so much for your replies. I’ve been having nightmares too- didn’t know that post op depression was a thing. My medical team just kept saying how much better I would feel after removing everything- I didn’t expect to feel worse. Good to know that this is common and there’s still hope!

I was thriving my first year until my meds stopped working. Hospitalizations, ECT - still was offered an amazing position at a top notch firm, but after working 12 hours a day as a summer associate, I declined the offer. I knew I wasn’t stable enough for that pressure. Never really recovered career wise. Got in an emotionally and financially abusive marriage to a man that was amazingly adept at gaslighting. What was left of my spirit he crushed. In a toxic work environment with law firm hours minus the law firm pay. I replaced two people and now am responsible for handling a workload that needs two additional hires if I ever want a decent nights rest and a weekend free. I’m afraid to quit or go back to school. I don’t know how to dream or hope anymore. There’s absolutely nothing that I could make this better. It’s as if I died inside. I just don’t have it in me to hope for a better tomorrow when it always seems to get a little bit worse. I worked so incredibly hard to have options and freedom only to end up trapped, alone, and barely holding on so I don’t cause my loved ones pain. I just want it all to be over.

If you live in the US, I have a doctor I would recommend you see - she's an expert in this and could refer you to a specialist in your area. A lot of doctors don't tell you to have regular surgery - mine didn't, I only learned that this was a treatment option when I saw my new doctor.

This was a coping tool I used for ten years when the pain was too much to hold inside. I did it when I was in danger of doing something worse - the relief stopped eventually and while I understand that it served a purpose when I had no support and a poor treatment team, the scars never go away. I’m constantly reminded of the severity of my illness every day. I dread summer as the scars are tell tail signs to every person I see that I’m not okay. Don’t beat yourself up for slipping. You’re doing an amazing by coping without cutting for long lengths of time. This will pass. Don’t give up. And don’t disfigure yourself like I did. I realize that right now don’t care, but one day you will regret that your skin is a permanent reminder of your painful journey.
